Apply a boundary crosswalk to tabular data

Source: R/crosswalk.R
ntl_apply_crosswalk.Rd

Re-expresses variables measured on the from vintage on the to vintage using an ntl_crosswalk().

Usage

ntl_apply_crosswalk(
  data,
  xw,
  id_col,
  vars,
  type = c("extensive", "intensive"),
  by = NULL,
  na_rm = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame keyed by the from identifier.

xw

An ntl_crosswalk.

id_col

Column of data holding from identifiers.

vars

Variables to convert.

type

"extensive" or "intensive", recycled along vars.

by

Additional grouping columns kept in the output, typically "period" or "year".

na_rm

Ignore missing contributors instead of returning NA.

Value

A data frame keyed by the to identifier (named as in xw) and by.

Details

  • Extensive variables (totals: output, population, sum of lights): x_to = sum(x_from * w_from).

  • Intensive variables (rates, means, shares): x_to = sum(x_from * w_to) / sum(w_to) over contributing units.

By default a result is NA if any contributing unit is NA, because a partial sum would understate the total.

Examples

ex <- ntl_example()
xw <- ntl_crosswalk(ex$units_old, ex$units_new, "district", "district_new")
stats <- data.frame(district = ex$units_old$district, year = 2022,
                    employment = c(120, 80, 60, 150, 90, 40),
                    unemployment_rate = c(5, 7, 6, 4, 8, 9))
ntl_apply_crosswalk(stats, xw, "district",
                    vars = c("employment", "unemployment_rate"),
                    type = c("extensive", "intensive"), by = "year")
#>   district_new year employment unemployment_rate
#> 1          D1a 2022         60               5.0
#> 2          D1b 2022         60               5.0
#> 3           D2 2022         80               7.0
#> 4           D3 2022         60               6.0
#> 5           D4 2022        150               4.0
#> 6          D56 2022        130               8.5
